newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia Budget - How the newspapers reacted.
newsitem.headline: Australia Budget - How the newspapers reacted.

text.p: Newspaper reaction on Wednesday to the Australian government's budget for 1997/98 was mixed to negative, with five of the six major newspapers generally judging it as devoid of the cuts and structural change needed to solve chronic unemployment.

The Sydney Morning Herald was most scathing, with one columnist describing it as a "confidence trick", while the most positive description came from Melbourne's Herald Sun tabloid newspaper, with its headline "Save up and cash in."
A selection of headlines, editorial comments and columnists views follow:
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW
Headline: "Costello's money-back guarantee"

Editorial: "In its first budget, the Howard government delivered a good first instalment in repairing the deficit flow out of the Keating government's last few years. Unfortunately, the second Howard-Costello Budget has failed to build on this momentum. The Budget handed down last night does virtually nothing to improve the Federal Government's structural fiscal position, instead opting to rest on last year's incomplete repair job."

Columnist: Alan Mitchell said in a column headlined "PM misses chance to build on last year" that the Howard government had "called it a day on fiscal consolidation, well before national saving has been raised to the level needed to repare the damage done by Labor's fiscal irresponsiblity."
THE AUSTRALIAN
Headline: "Costello rewards the savers".

Editorial: "The strength of Treasurer Peter Costello's second budget is its fiscal responsibility which offers the clear prospect of a return to a surplus. Its weakness is in its political thrust, directed at the next election. Mr Costello has set the scene for electoral vote-buying which would threaten the government's economic management achievements."
Columnist: Alan Wood said Costello's dilemma was obvious. "How do you deliver a good budget bottom line when your Prime Minister has no stomach for tough decisions."
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD
Headline: "A super shake-up"

Editorial: "It is a wasted opportunity. The ready-made savings created by delivering the co-contribution payment in the less costly form of a savings rebate has meant Howard and Costello have given in to the temptation to put the fiscal axe back into the shed."

Columnist: Ross Gittins said in a front page comment piece headlined "A savings confidence trick from Costello the conjurer" that the budget would reduce national savings rather than increasing them. "It is the budget of a government that knows what it should be doing but, after just one year and one budget, has lost the will to do any more."
THE TELEGRAPH
Headline: "Save your own bacon"

Editorial: Headlined "No cure for stunted growth," the Sydney tabloid said Treasurer Costello had "failed to to take up the greatest challenges facing our nation -- the urgent need for radical structural reform to the tax system and the demand for real flexibility in the workplace."
THE HERALD SUN
Headline: "Save up and cash in"
Editorial: Headlined "New Destiny for taxpayers", the Melbourne tabloid said Costello had delivered a solid budget, "but much more could have been done for the unemployed."
-- Canberra bureau 61-6 273-2730
